title: Ghost in the Shell
lede: Mamoru Oshii’s 1995 animated film of Masamune Shirow’s manga, set in a city modelled on Hong Kong, whose opening credits of computer code inspired the digital rain of The Matrix.
summary: Cyborg bodies, a Hong Kong-like city, and opening credits built from computer code. Mamoru Oshii, Production I.G, 1995.

source.label: Wikipedia: Ghost in the Shell (1995 film)

evidence.note: Based on the Wikipedia articles on the film and on cyberpunk, read as wikitext on 2026-10-02. No image of the film was inspected for this record.

styles.note: A canonical work of Japanese cyberpunk: the cyborg body, a Hong Kong-based city, and screen code as imagery. Wikipedia names it among the most notable cyberpunk anime.

context: Wikipedia: the city of the film was based on Hong Kong. Oshii felt that its streets, where “old and new exist in confusing relationships”, fit the theme of the film. [Cyberpunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk).

The opening credits were produced by CG director Seichi Tanaka, who converted code in a computer language displayed in romanized Japanese letters. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_in_the_Shell_(1995_film)).

The Wachowskis showed the film to producer Joel Silver, saying “We wanna do that for real.” The digital rain of *The Matrix* was inspired by its opening credits. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_in_the_Shell_(1995_film)).
interpretation: The film turns code itself into imagery. That is the source of the style’s terminal text used as decoration, which [The Matrix website](ref:whatisthematrix-website-2000) later made a web look.
Its city follows [Blade Runner](ref:blade-runner-1982) in taking Hong Kong as the model, which makes Hong Kong streets the most common real reference for the style.
